title: Brand Profile — the opinion carrier
description: The single file that turns the NEUTRAL engine into an OPINIONATED system for one brand. The engine holds no taste; this profile supplies it, and the checks enforce it, so after customisation the system rejects anything off-brand. Three layers meet here: a QUALITY FLOOR the engine always applies and no profile can switch off (accessibility, consistency, anti-slop); design MODELS the brand picks from CURATED options (so no choice can produce slop); and the VALUES/seeds a generator expands into an accessible token set. From this one file the engine derives the tokens, the per-brand rule set, the component skin, and the AI-legible layer (manifest/graph). It complements brand/brand.json (the Tier-1 strategy: mission, voice, personas); this is the Tier-2 design configuration. Paths/plumbing stay in dls.config.json.

schemaVersion.description: Version of THIS schema the profile targets. Lets the engine migrate old profiles.

profileVersion.description: Semver of the brand's own profile. A brand's opinion evolves; check-rules-compat treats a change to an enforced choice as a contract change, so bump this when one moves.

brand.description: Who the system is for. Strategy (mission, personas) lives in brand/brand.json; this is only what the design layer needs.

wordmark.description: The mark is an ASSET, never typeset. This points at the brand's supplied SVG(s); the engine renders it through the Logo slot and never reproduces it as text.

asset.description: Path/URL to the brand SVG (or a { light, dark } pair).

assetDark.description: Optional dark-surface variant; else the engine adapts by theme.

minWidthPx.description: Standalone legibility floor. In-app chrome uses a smaller size the engine derives.

voice.description: The copy layer of the opinion. Governs generated placeholder copy and the copy checks.

emDash.description: Copy policy for the em-dash — the clearest tell of AI-written prose. `avoid` is stricter than the engine's always-on density cap.

color.description: The colour opinion. `model` decides how many hues carry weight; `neutral` and `accents` are seeds a generator expands into full, ACCESSIBLE ramps (the engine derives APCA-safe steps for light and dark — a brand never hand-tunes contrast).

model.description: CURATED colour models. mono-accent: grayscale foundation + one accent for emphasis (2one's model). dual-accent: two coordinated accents. multi-accent: a categorical set. Each is pre-composed to stay coherent; free-form palettes are not offered.

tint.description: The grey is CHOSEN, not defaulted. A neutral biased slightly toward the accent reads as considered; a pure mid-grey reads as unconsidered.

seed.description: Optional neutral seed; else derived from tint.

accents.description: Accent seeds. COUNT MUST MATCH `model` (mono=1, dual=2, multi=3–5); the engine validates and, where a seed can't clear the contrast target as text/UI, auto-shifts it to a compliant step of the same hue.

seed.description: The identity hex; the ramp and accessible steps are derived from it.

role.description: What the accent is allowed to do. emphasis = links/focus/selection only (2one's discipline); primary-fill = may fill primary controls; decorative = broader use.

validation.description: Semantic hues, reserved for state. Always paired with a non-colour cue (icon/text) — that pairing is part of the locked quality floor and cannot be disabled here.

hues.description: Which validation hues the brand uses.

derivation.description: How the generator expands seeds into ramps. Accessibility here is not optional; it is the floor.

textApcaMin.description: APCA Lc floor for accent-as-text pairs.

uiApcaMin.description: APCA Lc floor for non-text (borders, focus rings).

themes.description: Themes to generate and audit. Both are the default; a brand may ship one, but each shipped theme is audited.

typography.description: Type is chosen from a CURATED, anti-slop-screened library, not a free-form font field. This is where the neutral engine refuses to hand a tenant the Inter/Space-Grotesk defaults that read as AI.

pairing.description: A vetted display+body pairing id. Each maps to two real faces (a characterful display, a readable body) known not to read as generic. 2one is grotesk-humanist (Satoshi + Inter). Custom brand faces are onboarded by adding a vetted pairing, never a raw font field.

ratio.description: Modular scale ratio the type steps are generated from.

labelCase.description: Case for section labels/eyebrows. `upper` everywhere is an AI tell; reserve it as an intentional accent.

shape.description: The radius/shape signature — the most legible piece of a brand's character on controls. A curated language, not an arbitrary radius, so the whole system stays coherent.

language.description: Control shape. pill = radius-full (2one's signature); rounded = a medium radius; sharp = near-square. The engine writes the radius scale from this and the check enforces it on controls.

base.description: The spacing unit. One base for the whole system; ad-hoc values fail the check.

density.description: Global rhythm; scales component padding coherently.

elevation.description: Shadow/elevation model. Shadows are neutral; coloured/neon glows are never offered (an AI tell).

decoration.description: The anti-slop policy layer. Defaults are restrictive because the tells (gradients, glows, emoji) are exactly what a neutral generator would otherwise reach for.

gradients.description: Decorative gradients. `forbidden` is 2one's stance (and the safe default); `emphasis-only` permits one intentional gradient; `allowed` opens it up. The check reads this.

library.description: One vetted icon set for the whole system. Mixed sets and emoji-as-icons are always rejected (floor).

motion.description: Motion budget. `functional` = purposeful micro-interactions only; blanket fade-in-everything and bounce-on-hover are not generated (tells).

enforcement.description: What turns TASTE into an OPINION. Each brand choice is bound to a severity; the engine emits the brand's ux-rules from this map, so `must` choices fail the build and `should` choices warn. This is why customising the neutral engine makes it strict.

choices.description: Severity per enforceable choice. Keys map to profile fields; values are the brand's chosen strictness.

qualityFloor.description: The engine's always-on guarantees. This is DECLARATIVE: the floor is enforced regardless of what a profile says, and `locked` records that a tenant cannot switch it off.

locked.description: Always true. The floor is not a per-brand choice.

includes.description: The universal guarantees every tenant inherits: accessible (APCA, both themes), consistent (one token system), anti-slop (no generic composition/copy), never colour-alone, one system across surfaces.

severity.description: How strictly the engine enforces this brand choice. must = a violation fails the build; should = warns; may = allowed escape hatch.
